title: A worked example: structured body-size model
text: simulate body-size dataset temperature (continuous), food (continuous, lognormal log(food) natural scale), sex (two-level factor), site (eight-level grouping). fitted model mean depending four predictors residual standard deviation depending temperature sex. symbolize() single entry point. pass biologically meaningful symbols (W_i body mass, T_i temperature, F_i food, S_i sex) units; rendered equations carry instead raw R names. Takeaway. One call symbolize() produces structured object; every later section renderer pulling rows .
code: library(symbolizer) library(drmTMB) #>  #> Attaching package: 'drmTMB' #> The following object is masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     beta  set.seed(20260523) n           <- 200 temperature <- runif(n, 8, 30) food        <- rlnorm(n, meanlog = 1.5, sdlog = 0.6) sex         <- factor(sample(c("female", "male"), n, replace = TRUE)) site        <- factor(sample(letters[1:8], n, replace = TRUE))  site_re <- rnorm(8, sd = 1.5) mu      <- 5 + 0.5 * temperature + 2 * log(food) +              3 * (sex == "male") + site_re[site] sigma   <- exp(0.3 + 0.05 * temperature + 0.1 * (sex == "male"))  dat <- data.frame(   body_mass   = rnorm(n, mu, sigma),   temperature = temperature,   food        = food,   sex         = sex,   site        = site )  fit <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(     body_mass ~ temperature + log(food) + sex + (1 | site),     sigma ~ temperature + sex   ),   family = gaussian(),   data   = dat ) sym <- symbolize(   fit,   symbols = c(body_mass = "W_i", temperature = "T_i",               food      = "F_i", sex         = "S_i"),   units   = c(body_mass = "g",   temperature = "C",               food      = "g/day"),   context = "structured body-size location-scale model" ) sym #>  #> ── <symbolized_model> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Class: <drmTMB> (drmTMB) #> Family: "gaussian" #> Response: "body_mass" (n = 200) #> Context: structured body-size location-scale model #>  #> ── Submodels ── #>  #> `mu`: `body_mass ~ temperature + log(food) + sex + (1 | site)` (link: #> "identity") #> `sigma`: `sigma ~ temperature + sex` (link: "log") #>  #> ── Equations ── #>  #>   W_i \mid \mu_i,\, \sigma_i \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i,\, \sigma_i^2) #>   \mu_i = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} \, T_i + \beta_{2} \, \mathrm{log}(F_i) + \beta_{3} \, [sex = \mathrm{male}] + u_{site(i)} #>   \log(\sigma_i) = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i + \gamma_{2} \, [sex = \mathrm{male}] #>   u_{site} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\, \sigma_{site}^2) #>  #> ── Symbols ── #>  #>   W_i                                         response variable #>   T_i                                         continuous predictor #>   F_i coefficients #>   --                                          mu submodel design matrix #>   --                                          sigma submodel design matrix #>   u_{site(i)} Reading mu row line line: \log(F_i) shows transformed predictor. bridge recognises log(food) transformation role renders transformation math, plain symbol. sex contrast renders \beta_{3} \, [sex = \mathrm{male}]. bracket notation contrast convention: coefficient applies whenever sex = male, female baseline folded intercept. random-intercept term u_{site()} appended mu predictor, flagged subscript depends site observation belongs . Spliced math-aware renderer (pkgdown site emits MathML pandoc; Quarto LaTeX renderers use KaTeX MathJax), two-notation block looks like : (index notation)Wi∣μi,σi∼Normal(μi,σi2)μi=β0+β1Ti+β2log(Fi)+β3[sex=male]+usite()log⁡(σi)=γ0+γ1Ti+γ2[sex=male]usite∼𝒩(0,σsite2)(matrix notation)𝐰∣𝛍,𝛔∼𝒩(𝛍,diag(𝛔2))𝛍=𝐗𝛃+𝐮log⁡(𝛔)=𝐙𝛄𝐮site∼𝒩(𝟎,σsite2𝐈8) \text{(index notation)} \begin{aligned} W_i \mid \mu_i,\, \sigma_i & \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i,\, \sigma_i^2) \\ \mu_i & = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} \, T_i + \beta_{2} \, \mathrm{log}(F_i) + \beta_{3} \, [sex = \mathrm{male}] + u_{site()} \\ \log(\sigma_i) & = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i + \gamma_{2} \, [sex = \mathrm{male}] \\ u_{site} & \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\, \sigma_{site}^2) \end{aligned} \text{(matrix notation)} \begin{aligned} \mathbf{w} \mid \boldsymbol{\mu},\, \boldsymbol{\sigma} & \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\, \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2)) \\ \boldsymbol{\mu} & = \mathbf{X} \boldsymbol{\beta} + \mathbf{u} \\ \log(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) & = \mathbf{Z} \boldsymbol{\gamma} \\ \mathbf{u}_{site} & \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\, \sigma_{site}^2 \mathbf{}_{8}) \end{aligned} Takeaway. mu line carries four predictors different roles (intercept, slope, transformation, factor contrast) plus random intercept, rendered symbolize() call.

Pasting output math-aware renderer (pkgdown site emits MathML pandoc; Quarto LaTeX renderers use KaTeX MathJax) shows proper math: (index notation)Wi∣μi,σi∼Normal(μi,σi2)μi=β0+β1Tilog⁡(σi)=γ0+γ1Ti(matrix notation)𝐰∣𝛍,𝛔∼𝒩(𝛍,diag(𝛔2))𝛍=𝐗𝛃log⁡(𝛔)=𝐙𝛄 \text{(index notation)} \begin{aligned} W_i \mid \mu_i,\, \sigma_i & \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i,\, \sigma_i^2) \\ \mu_i & = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} \, T_i \\ \log(\sigma_i) & = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i \end{aligned} \text{(matrix notation)} \begin{aligned} \mathbf{w} \mid \boldsymbol{\mu},\, \boldsymbol{\sigma} & \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\, \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2)) \\ \boldsymbol{\mu} & = \mathbf{X} \boldsymbol{\beta} \\ \log(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) & = \mathbf{Z} \boldsymbol{\gamma} \end{aligned} matrix form follows simple convention: bold lowercase vector (𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu}, 𝛃\boldsymbol{\beta}), bold uppercase matrix (𝐗\mathbf{X}, 𝐙\mathbf{Z}), Greek vectors keep Greek glyph. notation_bridge() educator-facing table pairs every piece model counterpart notation tags shape: Read follows: dimension column shape rule (\mathbb{R}^n, \mathbb{R}^{n \times p_\mu}), dimension_concrete column plugs actual sizes fit (\mathbb{R}^{80}, \mathbb{R}^{80 \times 2}). text: symbol_table() lists every symbol appears equations together role, units, dimension, description. Dimensions appear abstract concrete forms. assumption_table() distinguishes three statuses: stated assumptions formula (distribution, link, linear predictor); implied assumptions follow parameterisation (positivity σ\sigma, conditional independence); not_checked assumptions still user’s responsibility (missing--random). formula_bridge() translates R syntax mathematics. submodel R formula left, plain-English meaning, corresponding math notations. Takeaway. model says, assumes, R syntax maps math live three separate tables — reviewers can audit one independently.

text: v0.1 supports Gaussian random intercepts form (1 | group) first slice. symbolize() call works; equation set picks random-intercept term new distribution row, structured object gains random_effects variance_components tibble. mu linear predictor now carries +ugroup()+ u_{group()} term, new distributional row appears random intercepts: (index notation)Wi∣μi,σi∼Normal(μi,σi2)μi=β0+β1Ti+ugroup()log⁡(σi)=γ0+γ1Tiugroup∼𝒩(0,σgroup2)(matrix notation)𝐰∣𝛍,𝛔∼𝒩(𝛍,diag(𝛔2))𝛍=𝐗𝛃+𝐮log⁡(𝛔)=𝐙𝛄𝐮group∼𝒩(𝟎,σgroup2𝐈6) \text{(index notation)} \begin{aligned} W_i \mid \mu_i,\, \sigma_i & \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i,\, \sigma_i^2) \\ \mu_i & = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} \, T_i + u_{group()} \\ \log(\sigma_i) & = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i \\ u_{group} & \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\, \sigma_{group}^2) \end{aligned} \text{(matrix notation)} \begin{aligned} \mathbf{w} \mid \boldsymbol{\mu},\, \boldsymbol{\sigma} & \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\, \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2)) \\ \boldsymbol{\mu} & = \mathbf{X} \boldsymbol{\beta} + \mathbf{u} \\ \log(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) & = \mathbf{Z} \boldsymbol{\gamma} \\ \mathbf{u}_{group} & \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\, \sigma_{group}^2 \mathbf{}_{6}) \end{aligned} grouping structure exposed tidy tibbles, ready feed reports renderers: Takeaway. object carries everything reader needs discuss random structure — grouped, many levels, variance component goes submodel.
